findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Unretained mutable handing loses returned spend after native interruption and checkpoint restore
findings.smallest_reproduction: probe.py depths145/146 at recursion limit150, exact CPython3.12.3; no production patches.
findings.actual_result: Returned raw mapping holds spent account revision2; replacing mapping with revision1 and invoking original admitted action executes twice.
findings.expected_result: Returned spend prevents rollback redispatch; first interrupted verification does not accept.
findings.proposed_correction: Select stable execution-owner publication/lifetime contract; then implement it with interruption tests. Do not silently redefine handed to mean successfully captured.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Retained normalization omits owner JSON key transformation
findings.actual_result: Both ledger detail and experiment metadata numeric-key cases cause false permanent divergence after honest checkpoint restore.
findings.expected_result: The same owner-readable canonical history recovers.
findings.proposed_correction: Reuse full ordinary owner JSON transformation before retained entry hashing, preserving serialization semantics and exact barrier guard. Add both expected-acceptance regressions.

architecture_assessment.verdict: CONCRETE CONTRACT BLOCKER for complete arbitrary-interruption/all-returned-handings guarantee; does not block local MINOR fix.
architecture_assessment.reason: Once both captures abort and owner overwrites the sole mutable mapping entry, the follower has no retained reference to the spent version. Its recovery input is identical to the honest no-new-spend case. Returning acceptance may forget spend; permanent refusal without evidence poisons the honest case. Current API supplies no retained version or acknowledgement to distinguish them.

counterarguments.assessment: Could fix this precise recursion trigger; not demonstrated here. Starting/copying/publishing may itself fail or be interrupted before any stable version exists. Does not guarantee every returned mutable handing survives later replacement.

counterarguments.proposal: More retries or incremental per-map capture
counterarguments.assessment: Improves bounded windows, especially failure on experiments after ledger listing. Still fails before first retained reference when all finite recovery attempts abort.

counterarguments.proposal: Hold reader lock or retain raw mapping
counterarguments.assessment: Owner mutation does not share reader lock; raw mapping is exactly the mutable object replaced in executed proof.
No corruption evidence exists solely from interruption; violates stated honest-reader recovery requirement.

counterarguments.proposal: Owner immutable snapshot or retained publication until acknowledgement
counterarguments.assessment: Viable narrow generic integration remedy; requires selected owner lifetime obligation and publication/acknowledgement recovery semantics. No new budget authority is inherently needed, but this is not a reader-local reconciliation fix.

architecture_assessment.scope: Not a formal impossibility proof for every implementation/runtime; information-loss argument applies to current callback mutable-container contract and stated repeat-interruption model.
